subject.title: qualityGuard adopts the summary from the final compaction attempt even when it fails its own quality audit (not fail-closed)

question: When every qualityGuard attempt completes but the final summary still fails its audit, should safeguard compaction cancel with bounded recovery or accept a visibly degraded result?
rationale: Source proves the silent acceptance path, but current docs only define retries and repository history shows that unbounded cancellation can wedge sessions; the terminal reliability-versus-availability policy cannot be safely inferred.

options.title: Bounded degraded result
options.body: Accept the best candidate only as an explicit degraded outcome with audit-reason logging or telemetry and protection against repeated silent degradation.

options.title: Fail closed with escape
options.body: Cancel the failed compaction while adding a bounded escape or recovery mechanism so repeated malformed summaries cannot permanently block the session.

options.title: Document retry-only semantics
options.body: Keep accepting the final attempt and document that qualityGuard does not enforce acceptance, intentionally retaining the data-integrity risk.

recommendation.title: Bounded degraded result
recommendation.body: Accept the best candidate only as an explicit degraded outcome with audit-reason logging or telemetry and protection against repeated silent degradation.

likelyOwner.reason: This recent area contributor is the strongest available owner for choosing the core session reliability policy, with the original feature author providing design provenance.
